paragraphs.text: Expose a stdio MCP server (Playwright, Chrome DevTools, any MCP) as native DeepSeek Harness tools
# dsh-mcp-host
Expose **any stdio MCP server** as native DeepSeek Harness tools. Host-only plugin, no browser UI, n
MCP server** as native DeepSeek Harness tools. Host-only plugin, no browser UI, no npm dependencies.
Built for one job: let a DSH agent drive a browser through the official **Microsoft Playwright MCP**
server, attached to the Edge/Chrome you are already using.
> **0.4.0** — the browser tools unload when the browsing turn ends (and right after `edge_close`); l
ater requests carry only `edge_tools`. The MCP process and the open browser session stay alive, so r
eloading is one cheap call. See Unload after use.
## What it does
1. On load, spawns the MCP server once (default `npx --yes @playwright/mcp@latest --cdp-endpoint=mse

dge`) and calls `initialize` + `tools/list`.
2. Registers **one** bootstrap tool, `edge_tools` (name
configurable). Its description is deliberately short and states when to call it — and when not to.
3. When the model calls `edge_tools`, the bridge registers the real `edge_*` tools **for that Agent
only**, hides the bootstrap entry, and forwards every call to MCP `tools/call`. Screenshots are writ

ten to a temp file and returned as a path, not as base64.
4. **Unload after use**: when that turn en
ds (`session/event` → `turn/end`), the per-Agent tools are removed and `edge_tools` becomes visible
again, so every later request is back to one small schema. `edge_close` releases immediately, and an
idle countdown (`MCP_BRIDGE_RELEASE_MS`, default 3 min) is the backstop. The MCP process and the op
en browser session stay alive, so reloading is one cheap call. On `agent/disposed` (and on plugin di
spose) the same teardown runs.
Tools are renamed: `browser_navigate` becomes `edge_navigate` (prefix configurable).
## Lazy loading (default)
The 12-tool default set is **not** in the prompt until a browsing task needs it. A session that neve
r touches a browser pays for one small schema (`edge_tools`), not twelve.

- Set `MCP_BRIDGE_EAGER=1` to restore the old behaviour (register every tool at boot).
- Activation

is per Agent: the parent session and each subagent must call `edge_tools` independently.
- After act
ivation the bootstrap entry is hidden for that Agent (`tools.restrict({ deny })`), so the prompt goe
s back to a single, smaller surface.
## Unload after use (default)
Loading is temporary, so a session that browsed once does not carry twelve schemas forever:
- **Primary trigger: the end of the turn.** As soon as the session emits `turn/end`, that Agent's to
ols are disposed and `edge_tools` appears again — the next request only pays for the small bootstrap

schema. The next browsing turn reloads them with one call.
- **`edge_close`**: immediate unload (th

e page is closed, so the burst is over).
- **Idle backstop**: if no `turn/end` ever arrives (non-int
eractive hosts, long-lived agents), the tools also unload after `MCP_BRIDGE_RELEASE_MS` without a br

owser call. `0` disables the backstop.
- The MCP server process is **not** killed and the browser st

ays open — only the prompt surface shrinks, and reloading keeps tabs, logins and history.
- `MCP_BRI
DGE_RELEASE_ON_TURN_END=0` (with `MCP_BRIDGE_RELEASE_MS=0`) restores the 0.2.0 behaviour: tools stay
for the whole Agent lifetime.
## Default tool set (12 of Playwright's 25)
`edge_navigate`, `edge_navigate_back`, `edge_snapshot`, `edge_click`, `edge_type`, `edge_fill_form`,
`edge_press_key`, `edge_tabs`, `edge_take_screenshot`, `edge_evaluate`, `edge_wait_for`, `edge_clos
dge_press_key`, `edge_tabs`, `edge_take_screenshot`, `edge_evaluate`, `edge_wait_for`, `edge_close`.
Set `MCP_BRIDGE_ALL=1` to expose everything the server offers.
## Screenshots: image, path, or both
Playwright MCP ≥ 0.0.83 saves every screenshot to disk and returns text containing the path (`Screen
shot of viewport`), plus an image part unless told otherwise. The path is relative to the MCP server
's working directory (on this machine the profile dir) unless `MCP_BRIDGE_COMMAND` sets an absolute
ctory (on this machine the profile dir) unless `MCP_BRIDGE_COMMAND` sets an absolute `--output-dir`.
**This plugin never forwards that image part.** `normalizeResult` writes images to a temp file and e
very tool renders JSON text, so the model sees a path (~26 tokens), not an image. A screenshot has a
lways been cheap here.
So `MCP_BRIDGE_IMAGES` does **not** save context in DSH. What it buys:
- `MCP_BRIDGE_IMAGES=omit` — the upstream stops sending the image at all: ~12 K fewer base64 charact
ers over stdio per screenshot, and one less duplicate temp file. Pick it when the agent never looks
at the picture. **Caveat:** with `omit` the only path is the relative one inside the text, because t
he plugin's absolute temp copy (`images[]`) only exists in the default mode — an agent that wants to

open screenshots should keep `allow`.
- `MCP_BRIDGE_IMAGES=only` — keep the image, drop the accompa

nying text.
- Appended **only** to Playwright MCP command lines (`@playwright/mcp` or `playwright-mc
p`); other servers are left untouched, and an explicit `--image-responses` inside `MCP_BRIDGE_COMMAN

D` always wins.
- Default is unchanged (`allow`).
Context only suffers where a client renders MCP image content (Claude Code, Cursor, …): there a 1280
×720 capture is ~1.2k tokens. Those clients do not use this plugin — set `--image-responses=omit` in
their own MCP config instead.

## Install
From npm (published as `dsh-mcp-host`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
From a local checkout (development):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Restart DSH (or rely on hot-load) and open a new session. The default MCP command uses
`npx`, so Nod

e.js (which ships `npx`) must be on PATH; the first call downloads
`@playwright/mcp` from npm.
## Prerequisite for the Edge/Chrome you are already using
Open `edge://inspect/#remote-debugging` (or `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging`) and enable **Allow
remote debugging for this browser instance**. Then `--cdp-endpoint=msedge` (or `=chrome`) attaches
to that running browser with your logins and extensions. Without the toggle, Playwright launches a f
resh browser instead.
## Privacy
The bridge itself makes no network calls. It spawns exactly one child process (the MCP server you co
nfigured) and forwards bytes between it and the tool call. With `--cdp-endpoint`, the MCP server att
aches to your existing browser, which means it can see and act on the tabs you have open — treat tha
t as giving the agent your browser session.
